Seer.directive_trigger: players exhibit 'logic posturing' or 'mirroring' during the day
Seer.directive_rationale: prioritize your investigation on players who exhibit 'logic posturing' or 'mirroring' during the day to provide the village with an Anchor
Seer.actual_player_behavior: In Round 2 Debate, Riley used 'mechanical conflict' arguments to challenge the Seer. During the following Night 3, Hoang investigated Meg, who had been mirroring the Power Core's positions in Round 1 and 2.
Seer.verdict_notes: Hoang investigated the remaining suspects after identifying logic posturing/mirroring from Riley and Meg during the debate phases.

Guard.directive_rationale: You must prioritize the Seer to maintain the information pipeline
Guard.verdict_notes: Nhan protected themselves instead of the Seer (Hoang) during Night 1.

Witch.directive_rationale: you remained passive in the Day 1 debate. As a power role, you should help the village identify 'Vibe Traps' and support the PoE process
Witch.actual_player_behavior: Cong claimed the Witch role and actively contributed to the deduction by noting that Nam, Jin, Riley, and Meg had provided no deductive value and suggested narrowing the pool via PoE.
Witch.verdict_notes: Cong was active in the Day 1 debate and pushed for PoE.

Villager.directive_trigger: wolf uses villager terminology to frame others ('Pseudo-Logic' counter-attacks)
Villager.directive_rationale: be wary of 'Pseudo-Logic' counter-attacks—when the wolf (Meg) used your own terminology ('mechanical inconsistency') to frame others, you correctly stayed the course
Villager.actual_player_behavior: Riley (Wolf) used 'mechanical conflict' terminology to frame the Seer and Witch. Jin (Villager) identified this as 'pseudo-logic' and a 'Vibe Trap', continuing to vote for Riley.
Villager.verdict_notes: Jin recognized the wolf's use of pseudo-logic and stayed the course by voting for Riley.

Villager.actual_player_behavior: Nam and Jin both referenced the Power Core and the remaining pool of suspects to narrow down the wolves throughout the game.
Villager.verdict_notes: The villagers consistently used the PoE to isolate the wolves.

Villager.actual_player_behavior: Riley attacked Cong for attacking Riley's 'tone' and 'posturing'. The villagers (Nam, Jin) ignored this behavioral argument and focused on the role contradiction.
Villager.verdict_notes: Villagers ignored Riley's complaints about behavioral attacks and stuck to the factual role contradiction.
